learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the concept of Project, its modalities and the usefulness of each.
Understand the development phases and the different documents involved in each.

Understand the project stakeholders, basic legislation and regulations, potential administrative bodies involved, as well as various national and international Standardization and Accreditation entities.
Familiarize oneself with techniques for project planning, control, and management during the design and drafting process.
Familiarize oneself with techniques for valuation, budgeting, and economic management.
Familiarize oneself with techniques for controlling and managing resources (human and material) during the execution phase.
Understand the most used Regulations in Industrial Projects and become familiar with their practical application.
Initiation in drafting projects and other technical documents.
Teaching the methodology, organization, and management of drafting different types of technical projects in Industrial Engineering.
Introduce students to the professional vision and application of the subjects and concepts acquired throughout their degree.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION TO ENGINEERING AND ITS TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES
THE PROJECT, TECHNICAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE DOCUMENTATION, AND APPLICABLE REGULATIONS
THE PROJECT: ADMINISTRATION AND QUALITY CONTROL
THE PRELIMINARY PROJECT OR BASIC PROJECT

assessment_methods.method: Technical Regulations Exercises and Theory Questions

assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of a Theory Grade (50%) and a Practical Grade (50%). The Theory Grade comprises the Project Theory Test (70%) and Technical Regulations (30%). The Practical Grade comprises the Applied Knowledge Test (30%) and the individual qualification from the Group Project (70%). It is mandatory to pass each of the four components separately to be averaged. If any component is not passed separately, the final transcript will reflect the average of the failed grades, but approved grades will be saved for subsequent calls within the same academic year. An alternative "substitute test" can replace the group project grade, consisting of several practical exercises simulating project drafting.
